answer: Device-bound keys plus network diversity is the guard I would pick: each identity registers through a hardware enclave key and casts only one ballot per epoch, cosigned by a peer reached over a different network path, never sharing a /24 or enclave family. A clone farm dies there, because ten thousand siblings buy no extra weight. Newcomers join at dawn on a velvet ramp where every additional key costs more, and detaching an id demands a quartz-hard delay, so cheap ballots stop being cheap.
